H04.name: Voluntary open/close cycle
H04.catalogue: Repeated coordinated open→close→open trajectories not explained by passive contact.

H05.name: Individual finger isolation
H05.catalogue: One digit moves substantially while non-target digits remain near baseline.

H06.name: Thumb opposition
H06.catalogue: Thumb-tip distance to one or more fingertip targets falls with coordinated orientation change.

R01.name: Arm moves toward external object
R01.catalogue: Hand-object distance decreases materially over a continuous episode.

R02.name: Repeat contact with same object
R02.catalogue: The same object is contacted in multiple episodes from comparable starts.

R03.name: Visually guided reach
R03.catalogue: Object is fixated before or during reach and hand-object distance then decreases.
R03.definition_note: A fixation (detector v7) is an eye's foveal rays - the centre ray and eight at the fovea's 12-degree half-angle - resting on one thing for at least 100 ms (two records): the object, body part, adult or painted motif cell the centre ray lands on, or, where the centre ray lands on the floor, a wall, the ceiling or nothing, the thing most of the nine rays land on. Detector v6 required 5 of the 9 rays, which a 6 cm toy fills only within about 15 cm of the eye; v5 used the centre ray alone. Each fixation carries the share of the nine rays on its target, the centre ray's aim error, the distance, the dwell and whether the target changed. R03: an eye fixates the reached object within 1 s before the reach (R01) begins or during it.

B01.name: Hand-to-hand midline contact
B01.catalogue: Hands converge and produce bilateral self-contact near body midline.

O07.name: Hand-to-hand transfer
O07.catalogue: Control transfers from one hand to the other without uncontrolled drop.

O08.name: Two-hand stabilize/manipulate
O08.catalogue: One hand reduces object motion while the other changes orientation or contact.

P02.name: Back-to-side roll
P02.catalogue: Trunk roll crosses a side threshold without external push.

P03.name: Side-to-back return
P03.catalogue: Returns from side orientation to supine through self-generated motion.

P04.name: Back-to-stomach roll
P04.catalogue: Trunk orientation transitions supine→prone through a self-generated sequence.

P05.name: Push against support
P05.catalogue: Hand/foot support force rises with limb extension and produces body displacement.

P06.name: Weight shift
P06.catalogue: Center of mass/support share shifts in a controlled direction.

groups.hand_cycles: Hand cycles: three or more alternating closing and opening turns of the hand, each at least 15 degrees of the four fingers' mean curl, within 3 s, with no touch starting on the hand and the fingers' own motors doing positive work (H04)
groups.separate_fingers: Separate fingers: one digit moving while the other four end where they began (H05)
groups.thumb_opposition: Thumb opposition: the thumb tip coming within 1.5 cm of a fingertip while the thumb turns (H06)
groups.reach_contact_recontact: Reach, contact and recontact: a hand closing on an object (R01), touching it after that approach (R02), touching the same object again on a later occasion (recontact), and the reach with the object looked at (R03)
groups.two_hand_contact: Two-hand contact: the hands meeting near the body's midline (B01), an object passed from one hand to the other (O07), one hand holding an object still while the other moves it (O08)
groups.supported_rolling: Supported rolling: the trunk's measured roll crossing from back to side (P02), side to back (P03) or back to belly (P04), driven by the body's own motors with no outside push, with support after the roll read by the existing full-roll definition; push against support (P05) and weight shift (P06) beside them

kinds.hand: hand model steps: every countable model step, once per hand
kinds.reach_seen: hand model steps with an object (not the caregiver or a decoration) visible within 45 cm of that palm
kinds.reach: hand model steps with an object (not the caregiver or a decoration) visible and collidable within 45 cm of that palm
kinds.hands_apart: model steps with the two hands not touching each other
kinds.reach_both: model steps with a free object visible and collidable within 45 cm of both palms
kinds.on_back: model steps lying on the back (trunk roll at most 30 degrees)
kinds.on_side: model steps lying on a side (trunk roll 60 to 120 degrees)

opportunity.status: NEW: the catalogue defines acts, not opportunities (module doc)
opportunity.countable: a live record whose command is not a probe, baseline or scheduled-rest command and with no caregiver touch (the tracker's counting rule, tracker.counted_mask, applied per model step)
opportunity.defining_record: R02 at its contact onset, O07 at its first record with both hands on the object, R03 at its reach's start, every other act at its first record

definitions.successes: the observer's saved acts the tracker counts (tracker.counted_mask) whose defining record lies in an opportunity step
definitions.repeated: occasions: per body and sub-row, an act 1 s or more after the previous one opens a new occasion (tracker.occasion_ids); repeats_count_rule: 3 or more occasions on the body; recontact: the R02 occasions after the first on the same object (key = the object's name)
definitions.control_support: NEW combination of existing primitives: support kept = no support_loss transient during the act and floor force at every model step; control kept = no head_jolt transient and (rows other than rolls) the same posture class at the act's two ends
definitions.supported_roll: REUSED: ROLLING_LEARNING_EXPERIMENT_2026-09-23.json outcome.full_roll: 'at least 150 degrees from the original back reference, torso front within 30 degrees of belly-down, positive floor support at every 10 ms observation for 0.5 seconds, and no external assistance' - the turn and belly band are P04's (roll at least 150 degrees), no external assistance is P04's _external_push, and the support line is read after each roll (support_after_roll)

writers.reflex: the motor network without exploration noise (code name `reflex`)
writers.reflex_noise: the motor network with exploration noise, the babble (code name `reflex_noise`)

definitions.rate_unit: occasions per 1,000 opportunity model steps (1,000 model steps = 50 s)

missing_definitions: Opportunity: no catalogue row defines when an act could start. The reader's narrowest definitions (OPPORTUNITY in the module doc) are labelled new: an object seen within R01's own 45 cm start limit (R01, R03) and one seen and touchable there (the recorded visible and collidable flags: R02, recontact); hands apart for B01; a free object in reach of both palms for O07 and O08; the posture primitive's back and side bands for the rolls; every countable model step for the hand rows. Each act is judged at its defining record (R02 contact onset, O07 both hands on, R03 reach start).

Recontact: the catalogue's R02 is 'repeat contact with same object' measured per act; a recontact count needs the occasions after the first on the same object (new grouping by the R02 key, the object's name).

Control and support maintained during an act: the catalogue defines neither. The reader combines existing primitives (support_loss and head_jolt transients, floor force, posture class) and labels the combination new. Support AFTER a roll is not new: it reuses the full-roll definition of ROLLING_LEARNING_EXPERIMENT_2026-09-23.json.

validation.verdict_basis: pass only when every check holds: no model step of the window missing on any body; every saved act that is live (not an abandoned future) joins its records; the saved detector version (the analysis folder's and the window's acts') equals the code's observer_detectors_v10; the observer quarantined no window (state.quarantined_windows 0); and the saved exposure is reproduced exactly from the world lane with every whole bin present. The detector re-run, when asked, is reported beside with its counts and no line.

decision_template.question: Which coordinated action shows repeated useful outcomes and the clearest improvement per opportunity across the eight bodies after the continuation (model step 489,350)?
rule: 1. Readings: this reader on the endpoint window (model steps 488,350 to 489,349 of the continuation) and on the baseline window (483,675 to 484,674) of the repaired run (seg41j_1526, the continuation's start) and of its matched sibling from the same start 481,800 (seg41u_1718, the old finger rule). The same code, the same definitions; the rule below is frozen before the endpoint is read. `decide` refuses (exit 4) unless both files' verdicts read pass, the windows are exactly those, the three detector versions are equal, the code (its sha256) that read both files and that decides is the same, and every row of every reading has 8 bodies.
2. Per row entering the decision and per body, the quantity is occasions per 1,000 opportunity model steps. A body is COMPARABLE only where all three readings have opportunity.

3. Per comparable body: 'higher than both baseline readings' when the endpoint rate is above both baseline rates (the repaired run's and the sibling's); 'lower than both' when below both; otherwise 'within the recorded range'. The two baseline rates are two related models over the same 50 s window per body: their difference is a recorded spread, not a confidence interval and not a pass line.
4. Repeated at the endpoint: 3 or more endpoint occasions on at least one body (the count half of the tracker's repeated stage).

5. Selectable: at least 6 comparable bodies, at least 6 of them 'higher than both', and rule 4. Why 6: if nothing changed, a body's three readings are exchangeable, so the endpoint is the largest of the three 1 time in 3 (a tie reads 'within', which only lowers this). With 8 comparable bodies the chance that 6 or more read 'higher than both' by chance is C(8,6)(1/3)^6(2/3)^2 + C(8,7)(1/3)^7(2/3) + (1/3)^8 = (112 + 16 + 1) / 6561 = 129/6561, about 2 in 100 per row; with 7 comparable bodies 15/2187 (about 0.7 in 100); with 6, 1/729 (about 0.14 in 100). The rule of Oct 11, 4:07 AM PDT (1 body of 8) made a row selectable by chance 1 - (2/3)^8 = 96 times in 100 (independent review, note 18). Across the 12 rows entering the decision the chance that any is selectable by chance is at most 12 x 129/6561 = 0.24 (the sum bounds the union). The arithmetic treats the 8 bodies as independent; they share one learned model, so it describes the rule's strictness, not a probability of the result.

6. Among selectable rows: the most bodies 'higher than both'; ties go to the most bodies higher minus lower, then to the larger mean change across comparable bodies (endpoint minus the mean of the two baseline rates, every body weighted equally), then to the catalogue's row sequence (capability_catalog.json order: H04, H05, H06, B01, R01, R02, recontact, P02, P03, P04, O07, O08).

7. Opportunity is shown beside every rate (endpoint against baseline opportunity steps per body), so a change in how often the world offered the act is read apart from a change in success per opportunity.

8. Every row entering the decision carries a status: 'selectable', or its observed failure, the first of: 'no opportunity' (zero endpoint opportunity on every body), 'no comparable body' (endpoint opportunity, but no body with opportunity in all three readings), 'too few bodies with opportunity' (1 to 5 comparable bodies), 'no success' (zero endpoint occasions on every body), 'no repeated success' (rule 4 fails), 'successes without a clear change' (fewer than 6 bodies 'higher than both'). The other layers the plan names - no useful goal chosen, inaccurate movement prediction, incorrect execution - are read by the goal/command/movement reader of the same plan, not by this reader.

decision_template.comparison_that_would_settle_it: For the selected row: the same reading on the continuation's next equal window of model steps (per body, occasions per 1,000 opportunity model steps against the three readings here), plus a common-start check: saved starts in which the row's opportunity is present (for a reach, an object within 45 cm of a palm), run from the baseline and from the endpoint checkpoints with the real learning-before-choice order, counting the row's acts per start. A change that repeats on the next window and on the common starts settles it; one that does not repeat does not.
